  1. CITY COUNCIL AND PLANNING COMMISSION JOINT STUDY SESSION - DRAFT
  HOUSING ELEMENT FOR THE SIXTH CYCLE (2021-2029)

  The City Council and Planning Commission will review and provide input to staff on
  the Draft Housing Element, the primary tool used by the State to ensure local
  governments are appropriately planning for and accommodating enough housing
  across all income levels.

  2. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, October 5, 2021, at
  6:30 P.M. The next regular Planning Commission Meeting will be held on Tuesday,
  October 11, 2021. Information regarding matters to be considered at each meeting
  will be available on the Friday before the City Council and Planning Commission
  Meeting on the City’s website at www.sangabrielcity.com.

MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 30, 2021
  SPECIAL JOINT MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL

I  CITY COUNCIL AND PLANNING COMMISSION

  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Liao called the special meeting of the San Gabriel City Council and Planning
  Commission to order at 6:39 P.M. on Tuesday, September 30, 2021 , with all Council
  Members and staff participating by teleconference.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Vice Mayor Ding.

  ROLL CALL
  Council Members Present:  John R. Harrington, Denise Menchaca, Jason Pu, Vice
  Mayor Tony Ding, and Mayor Chin Ho Liao.
  Council Members Absent:  None.
  Commissions Present:  Mark Juarez, Anagh Mamdapurkar, Jerry Schwartz, Vice-
  Chair Jingbo Lou, Chair Thomas Klawiter.

I  Commissions Absent:
  Staff Members Present:
  None.
  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, Deputy City Attorney
  Martin Koczanowicz, Chief City Clerk Sharon Clark, and
  Acting Community Development Director/Planning
  Manager Samantha Tewesart.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS

  Chief City Clerk Clark provided information for the public on how to view the meeting and
  submit comments, and how to request meeting agendas.

  1. CITY COUNCIL AND PLANNING COMMISSION JOINT STUDY SESSION - DRAFT
  HOUSING ELEMENT FOR THE SIXTH CYCLE (2021-2029)

  The staff presentation was made by Acting Community Development Director/
  Planning Manager Samantha Tewesart and the consultant presentation was made by
  Jennifer Murillo, AICP, Senior Associate, of Lisa Wise Consulting, Inc. (LWC). LWC
  Director David Bergman was also present to answer questions.

I  Clarification discussion included site-inventory analysis methodology; housing stock
  inventory definitions of single-family detached units and single -family units; and
  median rent statistic methodology.

  Camila Alva Lopez, resident, and Norma Davalos, resident, provided comments in
  opposition to more housing developments.

  Mitchell M. Tsai, Attorneys for Southwest Regional Council of Carpenters, provided
  comments advocating the utilization of skilled and trained workforce policies and
  requirements.

  CITY COUNCIL SPECIAL JOINT MEETING MINUTES  Page 1 of 3  September 30, 2021
   Alice Wong and Family, residents, provided comments expressing concern about
  future potential multi-story housing developments and housing costs, and requested
  the topic be agendized for a regular City Council meeting.

  Anne and Stewart White, residents, provide comments requesting that the City Council
  preserve the character of San Gabriel.

  Sean McMorris, resident, provided comments in favor of: prioritizing affordable

I  housing needs over general housing inventory, streamlining the Accessory Dwelling
  Unit (ADU) application process, a Safe Parking Area for houseless people, preservation
  of current housing stock, and anti-displacement information dissemination.

  Senya Lubisich, resident, provided comments expressing concern over the impacts of
  Senate Bills 9 and 1O; requesting consideration of the Historic Context Statement in
  staff recommendations for potential housing sites; stating that increased density can
  be managed; and requesting that development be mindful of main traffic corridors
  and areas with higher rental and poverty rates, and recreational and open-space
  opportunities.

  Chuck Myers, resident, provided comments in opposition to eradication of R-1 zoning.

  Dr. Chasity Jennings-Nunez, HEAR Commission Chair and resident, provided
  comments in support of an inclusionary housing ordinance to require development
  with greater than 10 units to include at least 20% affordable housing and those with
  greater than 100 units to include housing targeting very low- and low-income renters.

  Debbie Kilgore, resident, provided comments expressing  concerns about a

I  development project on South Arroyo Drive.

  Discussion included that the City is not responsible for construction, only for creating
  an environment able to meet the state's housing allocation; methodology to develop
  more lower-income housing; exclusion of consideration of existing sites designated in
  the Parks Master Plan; a potential inclusionary-housing ordinance and current in-lieu
  fees; low-income units on religious-group property; anti-displacement information
  and its availability in multiple languages; possible effects of Senate Bills 8, 9, and 10,
  which will be discussed in greater detail in the October 19, 2021, City Council meeting;
  the City's ability to develop design standards for single-family zones; community-
  participation metrics and timing; the City Council having no control over state
  mandates, except the ability to make decisions regarding development projects;
  methodology for the maximum number of very-low and low-income units that the
  City can require in a project; objective versus subjective design standards; benefits of
  having an inclusionary-housing ordinance; purpose of a planned-development
  overlay; the need to plan for minimum density; whether inclusionary housing can be
  applied to R-1 zones; the City's need to show planning for SB 9 and 10 requirements
  in relation to the Regional Housing Needs Assessment (RHNA); percentage of San

I  Gabriel residents who are cost-burdened and related demographics; re-examining the
  Mission District Specific Plan for more flexible Floor Area Ratio (FAR), associated
  environmental impact aspects, and other factors; allowing for shared open space in R-
  2 zones; re-examining zoning to incentivize the market; peripheral programs such as
  emergency shelters, transitional and supportive housing, and Safe Parking, single-
  room occupancy (SRO) units; enhanced density bonus; standardized maximum height;
  and factors affecting San Gabriel 's housing situation.

  2. ADJOURNMENT

  Mayor Liao adjourned the meeting at 9:28 P.M .
